tasks.title: Reverse a String
tasks.description: Given string text, return its characters in reverse UTF-16 index order. Examples: reverseString('hello') returns 'olleh'; reverseString('') returns ''.
hints: Think about the last character first.
Collect characters before forming the final string.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The array-based reversal avoids repeated string concatenation.

tasks.title: Check if a String Is a Palindrome
tasks.description: Given string text, return true when it reads identically from both ends, otherwise false. Examples: isPalindrome('racecar') returns true; isPalindrome('cat') returns false.
hints: Compare matching positions from both ends.
Stop as soon as a pair differs.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Two indexes scan inward without allocating another string.

tasks.title: Find the Maximum Number
tasks.description: Given number array numbers, return its largest value, or null when it is empty. Examples: findMax([3,1,9,2]) returns 9; findMax([]) returns null.
hints: Use the first value as the current best.
Update the best only when a larger value appears.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: One pass retains only the current maximum.

tasks.title: Remove Duplicates from an Array
tasks.description: Given array values, return each distinct value once in first-occurrence order. Examples: removeDuplicates([1,2,2,3,1]) returns [1,2,3]; removeDuplicates([]) returns [].
hints: A Set stores only one copy of each value.
Converting the Set back preserves first-seen order.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The Set tracks the distinct values in first-seen order.

tasks.title: Count Character Frequencies
tasks.description: Given string text, return an object mapping each character to its number of occurrences. Examples: charFrequency('aab!') returns {a:2,b:1,'!':1}; charFrequency('') returns {}.
hints: Use each character as a key.
Start a missing key at zero before incrementing it.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The object stores one counter for each of k distinct characters.

tasks.title: Find the First Non-Repeating Character
tasks.description: Given string text, return its first character that occurs exactly once, or null when none does. Examples: firstUniqueChar('swiss') returns 'w'; firstUniqueChar('aabb') returns null.
hints: Count every character before deciding.
Scan the original order again to find the first count of one.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: A frequency map and two linear scans preserve first occurrence order.

tasks.title: Two Sum
tasks.description: Given number array numbers and number target, return indexes of the first discovered pair whose values sum to target, or [] when no pair exists. Examples: twoSum([2,7,11,15],9) returns [0,1]; twoSum([1,2],9) returns [].
hints: For each value, calculate the complement you need.
Remember indexes of values already visited.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The map makes each complement lookup constant time on average.

tasks.title: Find a Missing Number
tasks.description: Given distinct integers from 0 through n with one value missing, return the missing value. Examples: missingNumber([3,0,1]) returns 2; missingNumber([0,1]) returns 2.
hints: The complete range has a known arithmetic sum.
Subtract each observed value from that sum.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: It computes the range sum and subtracts each supplied value.

tasks.title: Move Zeros to the End
tasks.description: Given number array numbers, return a new array with nonzero values in order followed by all zeros. Examples: moveZeros([0,1,0,3,12]) returns [1,3,12,0,0]; moveZeros([]) returns [].
hints: Keep nonzero values in their original order.
Fill the remaining positions with zeros.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: A separate result preserves the input and holds every output value.

tasks.title: Find the Intersection of Two Arrays
tasks.description: Given arrays first and second, return distinct shared values in the order they first appear in second. Examples: intersection([1,2,2,1],[2,2]) returns [2]; intersection([4,9,5],[9,4,9,8,4]) returns [9,4].
hints: Put one array into a membership Set.
Use another Set so shared values appear once.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Two sets track membership and distinct output values.

tasks.title: Check Whether Two Strings Are Anagrams
tasks.description: Given strings a and b, return true when they contain the same characters with the same counts, otherwise false. Examples: isAnagram('listen','silent') returns true; isAnagram('rat','car') returns false.
hints: Different lengths cannot be anagrams.
Increase counts for one string and decrease them for the other.
A missing or exhausted count proves the strings differ.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: A frequency map compares the two strings without sorting.

tasks.title: Find the Most Frequent Element
tasks.description: Given array values, return the first value that reaches the highest frequency, or null when values is empty. Examples: mostFrequent([1,3,2,3,1,3]) returns 3; mostFrequent([]) returns null.
hints: Keep a count for every distinct value.
Only replace the answer when a count becomes strictly larger.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The map stores counts for k distinct values while one pass tracks the winner.

tasks.title: Chunk an Array
tasks.description: Given array values and integer size, split values into consecutive arrays of at most size items; nonpositive size returns []. Examples: chunk([1,2,3,4,5],2) returns [[1,2],[3,4],[5]]; chunk([1],0) returns [].
hints: Advance the start index by size each time.
slice handles a shorter final group.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Each input value is copied once into an output chunk.

tasks.title: Flatten a Nested Array
tasks.description: Given nested array values, return every scalar value in left-to-right traversal order. Examples: flatten([1,[2,[3]],4]) returns [1,2,3,4]; flatten([]) returns [].
hints: A nested array needs another traversal.
Append a value only after reaching a non-array item.
Call the same helper for every nested array.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Recursion visits every nested-array position and scalar once; n covers all visited positions and stack depth follows nesting.

tasks.title: Binary Search
tasks.description: Given ascending sorted number array numbers and number target, return its index or -1 when absent. Examples: binarySearch([1,3,5,7],5) returns 2; binarySearch([1,3,5,7],2) returns -1.
hints: The input must already be sorted.
Discard the half that cannot contain target.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Each comparison halves the remaining search interval.

tasks.title: Find the First Occurrence Using Binary Search
tasks.description: Given ascending sorted number array numbers and number target, return target's first index or -1 when absent. Examples: firstOccurrence([1,2,2,2,3],2) returns 1; firstOccurrence([1,2],3) returns -1.
hints: Remember a matching index instead of returning immediately.
Keep searching the left half after a match.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Binary search continues leftward only after finding target.

tasks.title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
tasks.description: Given ascending sorted arrays first and second, return one merged ascending array. Examples: mergeSorted([1,3,5],[2,4,6]) returns [1,2,3,4,5,6]; mergeSorted([],[1]) returns [1].
hints: Compare the next unmerged value from each array.
When one array is exhausted, append the other remainder.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The merge visits each input element once and creates the result.

tasks.title: Find Duplicates
tasks.description: Given array values, return each duplicated value once in the order its second occurrence is first encountered. Examples: findDuplicates([4,3,2,7,8,2,3,1]) returns [2,3]; findDuplicates([1,2]) returns [].
hints: Track values seen for the first time.
Use a second Set to avoid repeating duplicates.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Two sets retain seen values and distinct duplicates.

tasks.title: Find the Second Largest Unique Number
tasks.description: Given number array numbers, return its second largest distinct value, or null when fewer than two distinct values exist. Examples: secondLargest([4,1,4,3]) returns 3; secondLargest([7,7]) returns null.
hints: Track two distinct best values.
Ignore a value that equals either stored value.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: One pass retains only the largest and second-largest distinct values.

tasks.title: Rotate an Array
tasks.description: Given array numbers and integer k, return a new array rotated right by k positions; an empty array returns []. Examples: rotate([1,2,3,4,5],2) returns [4,5,1,2,3]; rotate([],3) returns [].
hints: A rotation amount can be reduced by the array length.
Build the result from the final segment followed by the initial segment.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Slicing creates a new rotated array without mutating the input.

tasks.title: Valid Parentheses
tasks.description: Given string text containing bracket characters, return true when (), [], and {} are balanced and nested, otherwise false. Examples: isValid('()[]{}') returns true; isValid('([)]') returns false.
hints: An opening bracket must be remembered until it closes.
The latest opening bracket must match the next closing bracket.
An empty stack is required after the final character.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The stack holds unmatched opening brackets.

tasks.title: Implement a Stack
tasks.description: Given operations as ['push',value], ['pop'], ['peek'], or ['isEmpty'] tuples, return one JSON result per tuple in order; push returns null and empty pop or peek returns null. Examples: stackTranscript([['push',1],['peek']]) returns [null,1]; stackTranscript([['pop'],['isEmpty']]) returns [null,true].
hints: The end of an array can act as the stack top.
Convert operations into JSON-safe result values.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: n operations are processed once and the array stores pending stack values.

tasks.title: Implement a Queue
tasks.description: Given operations as ['enqueue',value], ['dequeue'], ['peek'], or ['size'] tuples, return one JSON result per tuple in order; enqueue returns null and empty dequeue or peek returns null. Examples: queueTranscript([['enqueue','a'],['peek']]) returns [null,'a']; queueTranscript([['dequeue'],['size']]) returns [null,0].
hints: Keep a head index instead of repeatedly shifting.
Each operation must return a JSON-safe value.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The transcript processes n operations and retains enqueued values.

tasks.title: Fibonacci
tasks.description: Given nonnegative integer n, return the nth Fibonacci number with fibonacci(0) equal to 0 and fibonacci(1) equal to 1. Examples: fibonacci(0) returns 0; fibonacci(10) returns 55.
hints: The next value needs only the two preceding values.
Iterate rather than recursively recomputing values.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The loop retains only the previous two Fibonacci values.

tasks.title: Sequences and factorial
tasks.description: Given nonnegative integer n, return n factorial; 0 factorial is 1. Examples: factorial(0) returns 1; factorial(5) returns 120.
hints: Factorial starts at one.
Multiply each integer from two through n.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The loop multiplies each factor once while retaining one accumulator.

tasks.title: Removing adjacent pairs of characters
tasks.description: Given string text, repeatedly remove adjacent equal-character pairs and return the remaining text. Examples: removeAdjacentPairs('abbaca') returns 'ca'; removeAdjacentPairs('azxxzy') returns 'ay'.
hints: The previous unmatched character is the only one that can pair next.
Use a stack to remove a pair immediately.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The stack stores unmatched characters before joining the result.

tasks.title: Longest substring without repeating characters
tasks.description: Given string text, return the length of its longest contiguous substring with no repeated character. Examples: longestUniqueSubstringLength('abcabcbb') returns 3; longestUniqueSubstringLength('') returns 0.
hints: Maintain a sliding window with no duplicates.
Remember the latest index of each character.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Each window boundary advances at most n times and the map holds k characters.

tasks.title: Maximum subarray sum
tasks.description: Given number array numbers, return the largest sum of any contiguous subarray, or null when numbers is empty. Examples: maxSubarraySum([-2,1,-3,4,-1,2,1,-5,4]) returns 6; maxSubarraySum([]) returns null.
hints: At each value, choose between extending and restarting.
Track the best sum seen so far separately.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Kadane’s scan retains only the current and overall best sums.

tasks.title: Merging intervals while preserving the original array
tasks.description: Given interval pairs [start,end], return merged overlapping intervals sorted by start without mutating the input. Examples: mergeIntervals([[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]]) returns [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]]; mergeIntervals([]) returns [].
hints: Copy intervals before sorting them.
Compare each interval with the last merged interval.
Extend the last merged end only when intervals overlap.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Sorting dominates time; copied and merged intervals preserve the original input.

tasks.title: Minimum window length with a target sum
tasks.description: Given nonnegative integer array numbers and positive integer target, return the shortest contiguous window whose sum is at least target, or 0 when none exists; invalid inputs also return 0. Examples: minWindowLength([2,3,1,2,4,3],7) returns 2; minWindowLength([],3) returns 0.
hints: All values must be nonnegative for a shrinking window.
Advance the left edge while the sum still reaches target.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Both window indexes advance at most n times.

tasks.title: Group Anagrams
tasks.description: Given string array words, group anagrams by first-seen group order while preserving word order within every group; [] returns []. Examples: groupAnagrams(['eat','tea','tan','ate','nat','bat']) returns [['eat','tea','ate'],['tan','nat'],['bat']]; groupAnagrams([]) returns [].
hints: Use a representation that is identical for every rearrangement of a word.
A Map keeps insertion order, so create a group only when its key is first seen.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Sorting each of n words of maximum length k forms a grouping key, while the map stores the grouped words.

tasks.title: Product Except Self
tasks.description: Given number array numbers, return an array whose value at each index is the product of all other values without division; [] returns [] and a singleton returns [1]. Examples: productExceptSelf([1,2,3,4]) returns [24,12,8,6]; productExceptSelf([5]) returns [1].
hints: First put the product before each index into the output.
Walk from the right and multiply each saved prefix by the product after that index.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.spaceComplexity: O(1); auxiliary space excludes the returned output
solutions.rationale: Two linear passes use only prefix and suffix scalars besides the returned array.

tasks.title: Longest Common Prefix
tasks.description: Given string array words, return the longest prefix shared by every word; an empty list or empty word returns ''. Examples: longestCommonPrefix(['flower','flow','flight']) returns 'fl'; longestCommonPrefix(['dog','racecar','car']) returns ''.
hints: Compare characters by index instead of repeatedly creating shorter candidate strings.
Use the first word as the only possible full prefix.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.spaceComplexity: O(1); auxiliary space excludes the returned string
solutions.rationale: Each inspected character is compared until the first mismatch; n is the total number of inspected input characters.

tasks.title: Is Subsequence
tasks.description: Given strings needle and haystack, return whether needle's UTF-16 indexed characters appear in haystack in order without adjacency; empty needle returns true. Examples: isSubsequence('ace','abcde') returns true; isSubsequence('aec','abcde') returns false.
hints: Keep one position for the next needed character.
Only advance that position when the haystack character matches it.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: A single scan of haystack of length n advances one scalar index.

tasks.title: Linked List Cycle
tasks.description: Given nodes as {value,next} records and head as null or an index, return whether the reachable indexed chain cycles; every next is null or a valid node index. Examples: hasCycle([{value:1,next:1},{value:2,next:0}],0) returns true; hasCycle([{value:1,next:null}],0) returns false.
hints: Use indices rather than object references so the input stays JSON-safe.
Move one cursor one link at a time and another two links at a time.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Floyd’s two cursors inspect a bounded number of reachable indexed nodes.

tasks.title: Reverse Linked List
tasks.description: Given nodes as {value,next} records and head as null or an index, return a new descriptor with the reachable acyclic chain reversed without changing the input; an empty descriptor stays empty. Examples: reverseList([{value:1,next:1},{value:2,next:null}],0) returns {nodes:[{value:1,next:null},{value:2,next:0}],head:1}; reverseList([],null) returns {nodes:[],head:null}.
hints: Validate and collect the reachable indices before changing a copied descriptor.
The previous reachable index becomes each node’s new next link.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The reachable chain is validated once, then a copied descriptor and validation set are retained.

tasks.title: Tree Maximum Depth
tasks.description: Given a valid level-order indexed number-or-null tree, where children are 2i+1 and 2i+2 and trailing nulls are ignored, return maximum depth; [] returns 0. Examples: maxDepth([3,9,20,null,null,15,7]) returns 3; maxDepth([]) returns 0.
hints: For index i, the children are at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2.
The depth of a node is one plus the larger child depth.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The indexed DFS visits each non-null tree position once; h is the tree height.

tasks.title: Level Order Traversal
tasks.description: Given a valid level-order indexed number-or-null tree, where children are 2i+1 and 2i+2 and trailing nulls are ignored, return values grouped by depth; [] returns []. Examples: levelOrder([3,9,20,null,null,15,7]) returns [[3],[9,20],[15,7]]; levelOrder([]) returns [].
hints: Store indices for the current depth together.
Build the next depth from the two indexed children of each current node.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Each reachable tree node enters one level queue, and the grouped result is returned.

tasks.title: Validate BST
tasks.description: Given a valid level-order indexed number-or-null tree, where children are 2i+1 and 2i+2 and trailing nulls are ignored, return whether it is a strict BST; duplicates are invalid. Examples: isValidBST([2,1,3]) returns true; isValidBST([5,1,4,null,null,3,6]) returns false.
hints: A node must satisfy bounds inherited from every ancestor, not only its parent.
Pass a stricter upper bound left and lower bound right.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The bounds DFS visits each non-null node once and retains at most one root-to-leaf path.

tasks.title: Kth Largest Element
tasks.description: Given number array numbers and integer k, return the kth largest number, or null when k is outside the array length. Examples: kthLargest([3,2,1,5,6,4],2) returns 5; kthLargest([1],2) returns null.
hints: Keep only the best k candidates seen so far.
A min-heap makes the smallest retained candidate cheap to remove.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Each of n values performs bounded heap work while the min-heap never exceeds k entries.

tasks.title: Top K Frequent
tasks.description: Given number array values and integer k, return the k most frequent values by descending frequency and ascending numeric tie-breaker; invalid k returns null. Examples: topKFrequent([1,1,2,2,3],2) returns [1,2]; topKFrequent([4,4,5,5],3) returns null.
hints: Count each value before deciding the ranking.
Sort equal counts by the value itself so the result is deterministic.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The map counts n values and sorting u unique entries establishes the documented tie order.

tasks.title: Search Rotated Array
tasks.description: Given a rotation of an ascending array of distinct numbers and target, return target's index or -1 when absent. Examples: searchRotated([4,5,6,7,0,1,2],0) returns 4; searchRotated([],1) returns -1.
hints: At every midpoint, one half is still normally sorted.
Decide whether the target belongs to that sorted half before discarding the other.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Each iteration discards half of the distinct rotated array.

tasks.title: Daily Temperatures
tasks.description: Given temperature array temperatures, return for each position how many later days until a warmer temperature, or 0 when none exists. Examples: daysUntilWarmer([73,74,75,71,69,72,76,73]) returns [1,1,4,2,1,1,0,0]; daysUntilWarmer([30]) returns [0].
hints: Keep indices whose warmer day has not been found.
The stack should keep temperatures in decreasing order from bottom to top.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: Every index is pushed and popped at most once; the result and unresolved stack can each reach n.

tasks.title: Decode Bracketed String
tasks.description: Given text in count[fragment] grammar with ASCII letters and decimal counts, decode nested fragments; 0[fragment] returns '' and invalid brackets, counts, or characters return null. Examples: decodeString('3[a2[c]]') returns 'accaccacc'; decodeString('2[ab') returns null.
hints: Parse the bracket grammar before expanding any repeated fragment.
Represent zero-repeat fragments without rendering their children, while still validating their syntax.
Nested expansion must preserve the order of adjacent literals and repeated fragments.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.spaceComplexity: O(n + output * depth); includes AST, retained fragments, intermediate copies, and returned output
solutions.rationale: The parser scans encoded input n and builds an AST. Zero-repeat nodes are parsed but skipped during rendering; for positive nesting, retained intermediate strings can be copied at each of depth levels while output is the decoded length.

tasks.title: Generate Parentheses
tasks.description: Given integer n, return all balanced-parentheses strings for n pairs in lexicographic order; 0 returns [''] and negative n returns []. Examples: generateParentheses(2) returns ['(())','()()']; generateParentheses(0) returns [''].
hints: Track how many opening and closing parentheses have been placed.
You may add a closing parenthesis only when it cannot exceed openings.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.spaceComplexity: O(n); auxiliary space excludes the returned output
solutions.rationale: There are Catalan Cn completed strings, and joining each length-2n path dominates output construction.

tasks.title: Word Break
tasks.description: Given string text and dictionary string array, return whether text can be segmented into dictionary words; blank dictionary entries are ignored and empty text is segmentable. Examples: canSegment('leetcode',['leet','code']) returns true; canSegment('',['','a']) returns true.
hints: Build word prefixes once instead of creating a substring at every candidate boundary.
Let each reachable text index start a bounded walk through the trie.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The trie stores d total dictionary characters, and DP starts inspect at most L trie steps across n text positions.

tasks.title: Coin Change Minimum
tasks.description: Given positive integer coin values and integer amount, return the fewest coins needed; amount 0 returns 0 and impossible or negative amounts return -1. Examples: minCoins([1,2,5],11) returns 3; minCoins([2],3) returns -1.
hints: Let each amount remember the best answer found so far.
For a coin value, reuse the answer for amount minus that coin.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The table considers each positive amount against every supplied coin.

tasks.title: Course Schedule
tasks.description: Given nonnegative courseCount and [course,prerequisite] edges, return whether every course can finish; 0 returns true while invalid edges, self-cycles, and cycles return false. Examples: canFinish(2,[[1,0]]) returns true; canFinish(2,[[1,0],[0,1]]) returns false.
hints: Count prerequisites for every course before choosing a starting course.
Repeatedly remove courses whose prerequisite count reaches zero.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The adjacency lists and indegrees cover V courses and E prerequisite edges once.

tasks.title: Number of Islands
tasks.description: Given rectangular string array grid of '0' and '1' rows, return its count of four-directionally connected '1' islands without changing input; [] returns 0. Examples: countIslands(['11000','11000','00100','00011']) returns 3; countIslands(['0']) returns 0.
hints: Keep visited coordinates separately so the input strings are not modified.
When you find unvisited land, traverse its four-direction neighbors before counting another island.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.rationale: The scan and visited traversal each touch at most every grid coordinate.

tasks.title: LRU Cache
tasks.description: Given integer capacity and ['put',key,value] or ['get',key] operation tuples, return one result per operation using least-recently-used eviction; put returns null, missing get returns -1, and negative capacity returns []. Examples: lruTranscript(2,[['put',1,1],['put',2,2],['get',1],['put',3,3],['get',2]]) returns [null,null,1,null,-1]; lruTranscript(0,[['put',1,1],['get',1]]) returns [null,-1].
hints: A Map can locate a key, but it cannot by itself express recency updates efficiently.
Keep most-recent entries next to one sentinel and move a node whenever it is read or written.
When capacity is zero, puts still report null but no entry is retained.

solutions.label: Reference solution
solutions.spaceComplexity: O(capacity); auxiliary cache storage excludes the returned transcript
solutions.rationale: The Map and doubly linked list update, move, and evict one node per operation; auxiliary stored nodes never exceed capacity.
